segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Owen Vane gave up his dispensing book on one condition: that it be back on his counter by Friday, because half the parish's physic was written in it. Judith carried it down to the Bell before the light went.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Captain Farr was in the parlour, and Miss Hester Lamb with him, who had walked over from Upper Barton with eggs he had not asked for. He heard Judith through without once interrupting. When she came to the letter he set down his cup.

segments.speaker: Captain Nathaniel Farr
segments.text: April. And I was at Lisbon in April, learning to walk again.

segments.speaker: Miss Hester Lamb
segments.text: I read it. She brought it to our kitchen and I spelt the regiment for her, and she blotted the outside with her thumb. I thought it had gone.

segments.speaker: Captain Nathaniel Farr
segments.text: And she gave it into his hand?

segments.speaker: Miss Judith Vane
segments.text: At the kitchen table. He had taken charge of the post in March.

segments.speaker: Captain Nathaniel Farr
segments.text: Then I want Cobbold. His office has held my great-uncle's papers since before I was breeched. If there was ever an earlier will, it is on his shelf. I shall walk in Tuesday.

segments.speaker: Miss Judith Vane
segments.text: You will not walk eleven miles on that leg to be told to come back Thursday.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Mr Rowe had come in behind her, and had been standing by the settle for a full minute working himself up to something.

segments.speaker: Mr Silas Rowe
segments.text: Forgive me, Captain, but you are a soldier nobody has seen these seven years, with no money and a claim to three hundred a year. Any attorney in England hears that story twice a month.

segments.speaker: Captain Nathaniel Farr
segments.text: I do want the farm.

segments.speaker: Mr Silas Rowe
segments.text: Yes. That is precisely the trouble with it. But if Miss Vane went, with the book in her keeping and not yours, that is a ledger in the hand of somebody who gets nothing whatever by it. And Miss Lamb, who read the letter and will say so.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He stopped, appalled at himself, and looked at the floor. Judith looked at him for rather longer than he liked.

segments.speaker: Miss Judith Vane
segments.text: That is the first sensible thing anybody has said since Friday. I will go.

segments.speaker: Miss Hester Lamb
segments.text: And so shall I. It is my spelling on the outside of it.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Mrs Pike had it by nine the next morning, and gave her opinion in the Bell yard, where it would carry.

segments.speaker: Mrs Honoria Pike
segments.text: Eleven miles in a hired chaise, two young women and a gentleman this parish has not clapped eyes on since the year nine. I do not doubt any of you, and that is nothing at all to the purpose. It is what is said. Send the curate.

segments.speaker: Miss Judith Vane
segments.text: Mr Rowe cannot swear to my brother's hand.

segments.speaker: Mrs Honoria Pike
segments.text: Then send Owen.

segments.speaker: Miss Judith Vane
segments.text: Owen would shut the shop and go, and half the parish would do without its physic. Ma'am, I am six and twenty and I keep house for an apothecary. There is very little left of me to be ruined that Amberlight has not already had the pleasure of.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Mr Rowe paid for the chaise out of the vestry glazing money, and would not be thanked for it.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They went at ten. The near hind wheel had been complaining since the Alresford turning, and three miles short of the city it went. The chaise came down slowly into the ditch grass, Hester caught the dispensing book as it slid, and nobody was hurt at all.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The driver looked at what was left of the felloe, and threw a splinter of it into the ditch.

segments.speaker: Captain Nathaniel Farr
segments.text: Then what passes this road tonight?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Nothing, said the driver, till the market carts in the morning. And the wheelwright at Itchen Vale, a mile and a half off, would not come out after dark for any money in Hampshire.
